cloth_placement.rule: Clothes must be placed on the table before folding; folding on the floor is not allowed.

folding_assistance_scale.ambiguity: Rule 6 lists -100/-200 for minimal/partial help, but the score sheet lists -200 (main) and 5x-100 (additional) for flattening plus a separate percentage penalty up to -800/-400. Reconcile the two scales.

assistance.note: §5.4 rule 6 lists 'handing clothes to the robot' as reducing the score, but no quantified line exists on the sheet; §3.7.2 default applies.

entries.ambiguity: Assistance for handing clothes is named in rule 6 but unpriced on the score sheet.

assistance.note: §5.4 rule 6 names this as reducing score but the sheet has no line; §3.7.2 default (score zero) applies. Contrast with Pick & Place, where the equivalent appliance assistance is explicitly -0.

entries.ambiguity: Unpriced assistance. Decide whether this should mirror Pick & Place's explicit -0 treatment of appliance doors.

depends_on.note: Door may be opened with assistance; these points remain available.

assistance.note: Falls back to §3.7.2 default: assisted element scores zero.
Falls back to §3.7.2 default: assisted element scores zero.

entries.note: Basket must be placed in reach of the folding surface; requires two arms to carry.

depends_on.note: Only folded items can be stacked.

assistance.note: Major help completing the entire fold/stack carries the maximum penalty (§5.4 rule 6).

gpsr.method_note: Entries are the fixed primitives a generated command is scored against; the command generator composes them at runtime.

reductions_apply_to: receiving human assistance to accomplish a command
instructing a human assistant to perform the whole task
autonomy_skip.ambiguity: The last two are declared to incur reductions but have no quantified line on the score sheet. Either add explicit entries or state that §3.7.2 (score zero) governs.

assistance.note: Custom operator available only after the referee attempts three re-phrased commands.

entries.ambiguity: Fixed 3x-20 (-60, ~4% of 1490) conflicts with §3.7.4, which sets custom operator at -10% of maximum attainable score (-149). Confirm which governs.

depends_on.note: Command may be acquired via custom operator or ASR bypass; planning remains scoreable.

entries.ambiguity: Fixed 3x-50 (-150, ~10%) vs §3.7.4 gesture/alternative-HRI rates of -20% of max attainable. Confirm interaction.

custom_operator.note: Since the main focus of the test is HRI, no custom operator can be chosen.

alternative_hri.note: Score reduction per information (name or favorite drink).

assistance.note: Waiting for the doorbell is optional; robots may bypass it and meet the guest at the door. Bypassing is an alternative strategy, not assistance.

entries.note: Scored only if robot waits at starting position and reacts instantly.

assistance.note: Entrance door is open by default; team leader may request it closed to make these points available. Referee opens on request (§5.1 Referee Instructions).

entries.note: Opportunity is opt-in: points only exist if the team requests a closed door.
Awarded only if the robot continuously tracks the moving person.

depends_on.note: Guest must be escorted to the living room first.

entries.note: Robot must clearly indicate or point to a location or seat.
Asking a guest to repeat because the robot could not hear is not a non-essential question.

depends_on.note: Information may be obtained via alternative HRI at -20 per item.

assistance.note: Alternative HRI to understand a guest causes a reduction per information item.

depends_on.note: Both guests must be seated before introductions.

assistance.note: Two distinct assisted modes are priced separately (-25 asking for help, -50 bag placed on structure). Neither blocks the follow/drop chain.

entries.note: Max points require: robot signals readiness, manipulator within 10 cm of operator's hand, operator completes the handover.

entries.ambiguity: §5.1 rule 5 says 'no points are awarded' for this route, and the sheet also applies -50. Confirm whether both forfeiture and penalty are intended, or only the penalty.

depends_on.note: Robot may carry the bag by any assisted route; following is scoreable regardless.

assistance.note: Four penalized recovery forms listed in §5.1 rule 4.

depends_on.note: Robot must be holding the bag; assisted acquisition still permits this line.

assistance.note: Falls back to §3.7.2 default: assisted element scores zero.

entries.ambiguity: Fixed -20 per item here, but §3.7.4 prices alternative HRI at up to -20% of max attainable score (=-290). Confirm which governs.

sequence.note: No predefined sequence; but pouring and closing the dishwasher must occur after prerequisite steps to be scored.

assistance.note: Pointing to objects is listed assistance in §5.2 rule 15.

entries.note: Robot must clearly communicate perception to the referee (§5.2 rule 16).

assistance.note: Handover assistance forfeits this line (-0 self) and costs -100; placing remains available.

depends_on.note: Bonus requires an autonomous first pick.

entries.note: Deliberate negative pricing of an easy pick; acts as an Entry-Level discount rather than a tier.

depends_on.note: Object must be in hand; assisted handover still permits placing.
Door may be opened by referee at no cost (-0); these points remain fully available.
Rack may be pulled by referee at no cost (-0).

entries.note: Items must be positioned as a human would and be cleanable by the machine (§5.2 rule 9).

assistance.note: Falls back to §3.7.2 default: assisted element scores zero.
Explicitly free (-0). Assisted execution forfeits this line only.
Explicitly free (-0). Reward is defined as autonomous ('without assistance').

entries.ambiguity: Single entry bundles opening and closing, which have different preconditions: §5.2 rule 8 awards closing points only after at least one item has been placed inside. Consider splitting MAN-OPERATE-02 into opening and a new closing line (depends_on MAN-PLACE-02B1).

assistance.note: Explicitly free (-0); robot must clearly ask for help (§5.2 rule 13).

depends_on.note: Milk container may be opened by referee at no cost; pouring points remain available.
§5.2 procedure 5: pouring must occur after prerequisite placing steps to be scored.

entries.note: A significant amount must be poured; a few drops or bits is not enough.

entries.ambiguity: Count is 24 (2x the 12 picks). Confirm whether this is intended as pick+place handovers counted separately.

entries.note: Applied per item / per group of nearby items moved (§5.2 rule 15).

restart.note: All points earned before the restart are voided; scoring resumes from zero.

barman_assistance.note: The Professional Barman assists on request; robot may use up to two minutes to instruct the barman per order. If requested, the barman will place the order in a basket or tray.

disqualifying.description: Touching the robot after the start signal

emergency_stop.note: A TC member follows the robot ready to press the emergency stop button; any physical contact with people or furniture results in immediate emergency stop.

assistance.note: If the robot detects a customer but does not reach the table, it must clearly identify the person to earn partial points.

depends_on.note: Partial credit available if the table is not reached but the customer is identified.

entries.ambiguity: Fixed -80 per order vs §3.7.4's -20% of max attainable (-472). Confirm which governs.

assistance.note: Barman handover forfeits this line and costs -100; serving remains available.

depends_on.note: Items may be acquired via barman handover; serving remains scoreable.
Tray is one transport route, not required.

assistance.note: All delivered objects must be placed on the customer's table.
If requested, the barman will place the order in a basket or tray for the robot to deliver.

entries.note: Requires placing items on tray, picking up and transporting the tray, then delivering.
